page: Amazon Web Services r8ib.48xlarge is a memory-optimized cloud server instance built on the Nitro hypervisor and powered by x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors. The instance provides 192 dedicated vCPUs across 96 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at up to 3.9 GHz, backed by 480 MB of shared L3 cache and hardware support for AMX and AVX-512 vector extensions. Memory capacity measures 1536.0 GB of high-frequency DDR5 running at 7 GHz, delivering an 8 GB per vCPU allocation. Network connectivity is anchored by a 200 Gbps baseline interface. The instance does not include bundled local storage and contains no discrete GPUs, utilizing remote storage volumes over the network for persistent data.

Synthetic and application benchmarks place the r8ib.48xlarge among top-tier performers for parallel throughput and memory operations. While single-thread CPU performance operates in the average range, multi-core stress-ng tests achieve top-decile throughput due to the high core count. Memory subsystem evaluation reveals large-block uncached read speeds of 574.65 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 236.03 GB/sec. Application testing demonstrates high transactional capacity, achieving 270.1 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 310.49 GB/sec in static web throughput. In CPU-based machine learning inference, the architecture delivers top-tier prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and 70-billion-parameter language models, accelerated by Intel AMX matrix instructions.

From an efficiency perspective, the r8ib.48xlarge provides dense memory and high network throughput per host, enabling consolidation of distributed in-memory nodes into a unified environment. The primary architectural tradeoff centers on the absence of attached local NVMe drives, requiring high-IOPS applications to interact with remote storage services across the 200 Gbps network fabric. This instance is suited for in-memory databases like Redis, massive enterprise database deployments, real-time analytics pipelines, enterprise ETL processing, and large-scale CPU-based inferencing tasks.
